source.title: Scaling Laws for Physics-Aware ACOPF Surrogate Learning
source.authors: Yi-Jiang Li; Emon Dey; Stefano Fenu; Massimiliano Lupo Pasini; T. Kuruganti; Kibaek Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study measures scaling in a distinct scientific-learning setting and shows that fitted model–data exponents differ with the training objective; its authors characterize the estimates as local to the tested range.
record.gate_note: The study tests scaling relationships for ACOPF surrogates, not language-model pretraining loss. It does not test small-run extrapolation, a compute-optimal parameter/token split, architecture-shape sensitivity, or downstream-task predictability. The training-cost comparison is not itself a scaling-law result. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws in model size and unique-sample count for HGT ACOPF surrogates, a regime outside text pretraining, so its results bear on V5. It also compares fitted exponents across training objectives, which bears weakly on V7. This makes it a new setting with a result on the claim (T3) rather than a challenge to a version (T5). It reports no language-model loss, compute-optimal split, shape sweep or downstream result. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. On case2000, both objectives improve as power laws in N and D over the tested range. MSE prediction loss is model-dominant (0.949, 0.596), while the AL composite score is balanced (0.284, 0.292); the exponents are local. Violation grows with network size much more slowly under AL (exponent 0.513 vs 1.196), while prediction error grows comparably under both objectives. At equal samples, AL cuts violation about 19× at 2.4× training time, with negligible extra memory. The authors conclude the objective shapes scaling behavior, not only final performance.
record.recipe_differences: This is a scientific-surrogate scaling study using HGT, ACOPF prediction loss and constraint violation, and log-space fits; it does not reproduce language-model pretraining or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The training objective changes the fitted model–data exponents: MSE prediction loss is more dependent on model size, while the AL composite score has nearly equal model and data exponents. Physical network size also affects constraint-violation growth differently under MSE and AL.

fits_no_version.finding: Topology-normalized constraint violation grows with bus count at k=1.196 under MSE and k=0.513 under AL. The gap is largest for active-power balance, about half as large for reactive balance, and nearly absent for line limits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Physics-aware AL training reduces the growth rate of ACOPF constraint violation with network size at fixed model and data budget, non-uniformly across constraint types.

fits_no_version.finding: Prediction error grows with network size comparably under MSE and AL, according to the authors' text; no numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction error of ACOPF surrogates worsens with physical network size similarly across MSE and AL objectives.

record.problems: The model–data sweep uses one architecture family, one topology, and a single fixed seed; it spans 6.7× in model size and 5× in dataset size. Bootstrap intervals reflect fit uncertainty, not seed-to-seed variability. The authors state that the exponents are effective local exponents and that an irreducible floor was not identifiable from the tested grid. Cross-topology prediction-error values are described in text without numerical exponents.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling results left out. The matched-sample and matched-prediction-loss cost comparisons in Section V-C were not included because they do not measure the scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss in any form.
Extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs; no held-out larger run is predicted.
Fixed-compute allocation and compute-optimal N/D growth.
Shape at fixed N; depth and heads are held fixed and only hidden dimension varies.
Power laws over several orders of magnitude: the range is only 6.7× in N and 5× in D. Also untested: image/video, fine-tuning, transfer, other architectures, topologies and seeds.
Parameter-counting conventions, training schedule, and different datasets. Curve bending away from a power law is not observed or tested.

missing.what: Sensitivity fit with the additive Chinchilla form L=E+AN^-α+BD^-β. Fitted E was typically at or near zero, and exponent bootstrap intervals were broad, so no stable irreducible floor was identifiable. This bears on fitting-method dependence and on how firm the exponents are.
missing.locator: Section V-A, paragraph after Table I

missing.what: Bootstrap interval for αN−βD excludes zero under MSE and includes zero under AL.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T3: this is a new-domain test that finds power laws, not an argument that a version is wrong. Main caveats for V5: under one decade on each axis, a single seed, one topology and one architecture, and joint-fit R²log of 0.86–0.90. Training is multi-epoch with samples-seen held fixed across model sizes, so D counts unique samples under repetition. Section V-C cost comparisons are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from smaller runs predict the loss of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token growth trends.
Architecture shape is fixed; depth, width, and other architecture choices are not compared at fixed parameter count.
Tests model–data scaling for ACOPF surrogates, not image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other scientific tasks.

The study compares training objectives, but does not test alternative parameter-counting conventions, schedules, datasets, or fitting methods as causes of differing laws; it does not observe curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: HGT (model–data sweep; aggregate fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit prediction loss against dataset size at fixed model size
rows.value: LMSE(D) = 0.008 (D / 1.44 × 10^5)^−0.843; R²log = 0.950. Increasing the training set from 48K to 240K reduces validation loss by approximately 74%.
rows.note: The authors describe the observed relationship as power-law behavior.

relationships.condition: HGT ACOPF surrogates on case2000, 100M–671M params and 48K–240K samples, under the MSE and AL objectives, single seed
relationships.reason: Single-axis fits have R²log 0.94–0.98 and joint fits 0.86–0.90, with monotone declines (R1–R6). The range is under one decade and the authors call the exponents local.
relationships.display_finding: Errors declined monotonically, with single-axis log-space R²=0.94–0.98 and joint R²=0.86–0.90 over less than one decade, yielding exponents described as local.

relationships.display_finding: αN was 0.949 under MSE versus 0.284 under AL with non-overlapping confidence intervals, although the fitted metric also differed; an additive fit left the floor unidentifiable and exponent intervals broad.
